title: Fulcrum Search - Embeddings & Rerank discovery
summary: Discovery call to understand Fulcrum's current search stack, planned rerank flow, scale targets (1M-10M vectors), latency/cost targets, and security requirements. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs for embeddings and ANN, index choices (HNSW/IVFPQ), hybrid sparse+dense approaches, and a proposed benchmark pilot. Next steps: send pricing/security docs, share benchmark spreadsheet, schedule pilot with sample dataset.
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing sheet and Dedicated sizing options
Redwood SE to share security and SOC2 docs
Fulcrum to provide a sample of 200k vectors and query set for pilot
Schedule a 2-hour benchmark run with Redwood Dedicated (pilot) week of 2026-07-13
action_items: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE): email pricing + Dedicated/Private comparison (due: 2026-07-02)
Marco Diaz (Redwood SE): share benchmark spreadsheet and sample infra runbook (due: 2026-07-01)
Asha Banerjee (Fulcrum): export and share 200k vector sample + 500 query workload (due: 2026-07-06)
Tom Reed (Fulcrum): confirm security contacts and preferred cloud region (due: 2026-07-02)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE); Marco Diaz (Redwood SE); Priya Patel (Fulcrum Head of Search); Tom Reed (Fulcrum SRE); Asha Banerjee (Fulcrum ML Eng)

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sophie from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Marco, our solutions engineer. Quick intro then we'll jump into your current stack.
[00:12] Priya: Hi Sophie, hi Marco - thanks. I'm Priya, I lead search at Fulcrum. We have Tom and Asha on the call to cover infra and the model work.
[00:20] Tom: hey
[00:22] Asha: morning, thanks for fitting us in.
[00:28] Sophie: Great. The goal for today is to understand your rerank pipeline, vector DB choices, scale targets, and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense. We'll also talk benchmarks and next steps. Does that align?
[00:36] Priya: yep, that's it. We're redoing our embeddings/re-rank stack - current infra is elasticsearch for sparse signals and a managed vector DB for dense, but cost/latency are blowin up.
[00:48] Marco: quick clarifying q - when you say managed vector DB, which one? and what's your current embedding dim and model?
[00:55] Asha: we're on Pinecone for vectors, embedding dim is 1536 from OpenAI-text-embedding-3-small-ish - actually we tried a couple; 1536 gives best quality. Throughput is around 800 qps at peak, but most queries are spikes. Latency target for the whole page (sparse + dense + rerank) is sub-150ms p90 ideally.
[01:18] Sophie: ok that's helpful. So two parallel concerns: cost at 800 qps spikes and latency. Also you mentioned a rerank - is that a second-stage transformer scoring top-K?
[01:27] Priya: correct. We do BM25 to shortlist, then ANN to get dense top 200, then a cross-encoder reranker on top-32. Reranker is expensive - it runs on CPU today and adds 60-120ms depending on batch.
[01:40] Marco: got it. A few things we'll typically discuss: embedding generation (hosted vs bring-your-own), where ANN/indices run (dedicated GPUs vs CPU instances), and hybrid search patterns - e.g., BM25 + HNSW followed by IVFPQ for large recall sets.
[01:56] Asha: For accuracy, the reranker is important. We can't sacrifice it. But we also know we can tune embedding dim. Is 1536 overkill for production?
[02:06] Marco: short answer: sometimes. 768-1024 dims often hit a good quality/cost sweet spot depending on your training data. We usually recommend running an eval sweep: downsample your corpus and measure MRR/NDGC vs embedding dims. We can help run that as part of the pilot.
[02:20] Priya: ok yeah we'll want that. On the vector DB side, the managed vendor charges a lot for storage and also for throughput - do you host an index or integrate with their DB?
[02:31] Sophie: Redwood supports multiple modes. For quick POC you can use our Hosted embeddings + our ANN (we run Faiss/HNSW on GPUs in the backend). For production at your scale with predictable throughput, Dedicated is common - you get reserved GPU pools and predictable latency and cost per qps. Private is for VPC/on-prem when security/compliance requires it.
[02:55] Tom: security is a hard requirement - SOC2 and audit logs, and we'd prefer private control plane if possible, but that's heavier. Is Redwood Private available as a managed appliance?
[03:06] Marco: yes, Private supports VPC deployments and on-prem with customer-managed networking. We integrate with KMS for key management and keep audit logs. For pilot though many customers do Dedicated in the cloud to validate perf before moving Private.
[03:18] Asha: curious about the rerank runtime - do you recommend running cross-encoder on GPU to hit p90 targets? Right now CPU time kills us.
[03:25] Marco: GPUs will help a lot. For cross-encoder rerank we usually run batches on GPU and use mixed precision/quantization where possible. Also, you can reduce top-K to 64 and use a cheap reordering model to prune before cross-encoder. We can demo batching improvements that reduce per-request compute.
[03:40] Priya: our budget is tight though. Are there configurations where we host embeddings with Redwood Hosted but keep reranker in-house?
[03:48] Sophie: absolutely. You can use Redwood Hosted for embedding generation and ANN search while keeping the rerank layer in your environment - or vice versa. We also offer hybrid routing so high-priority traffic goes to Dedicated and overflow to Hosted.
[03:59] Tom: can you talk throughput numbers - like how many qps per GPU for the ANN index? We need to estimate size and pool.
[04:07] Marco: depends on dim and index type. Rough ballpark: for 1536-dim float32 HNSW on a modern A100 or equivalent, you can get several thousand qps for vector-only retrieval at p95 < 10ms with batching and prefix cache. If you move to IVFPQ with aggressive quantization, you can handle larger scale with lower memory but higher CPU/GPU per-query overhead - it's a tradeoff. For Dedicated we size by expected sustained qps and tail latency SLO.
[04:33] Asha: huh. We're storing ~3.2M embeddings currently but planning to grow to 10M. Index memory is a concern - can Redwood do quantized indices?
[04:42] Marco: yes, we support PQ/OPQ/IVFPQ and 8-bit/4-bit quantization for embeddings on certain execution paths. The runtime will pick kernels optimized for quantized ops; quality drop is workload-dependent. We'll run a quality vs size sweep in the pilot.
[04:58] Priya: about hybrid search - we currently run BM25 then ANN. We're evaluating sparse+dense fusion at ranking time. Any best practices?
[05:06] Marco: common pattern: use BM25 to get high recall shortlists, use dense ANN for semantic recall, then concatenate features for a learning-to-rank model or cross-encoder. For hybrid, you can also do reweighting via lambda parameters or use late-fusion. We saw many customers use an elasticsearch+vector DB combo with light-weight feature stitching in the reranker. Redwood's routing and trace hooks make it easy to observe per-step latencies.
[05:31] Tom: how does Redwood integrate with existing vector DBs? We don't want to rip and replace Pinecone yet.
[05:36] Marco: two ways: 1) Redwood can act as the embedding generation and ANN host and you migrate indices into Redwood, or 2) you keep Pinecone and we do inference and rerank in place - we can call out to embeddings and pull vectors for rerank flows. For benchmarking we typically ingest a sample into our environment to measure pure perf.
[05:53] Asha: we'd like to avoid full migration at first. So option 2 sounds better. Can you do hybrid - use Pinecone for storage but run hot indices on Dedicated?
[06:01] Sophie: yes, we can set up a tiering strategy. Cold data stays in your vector DB, hot partitions can be hosted on Dedicated for low-latency queries. Redwood supports routing policies by region and capacity so you can keep cost lower.
[06:12] Priya: nice. On evaluation metrics: we need MRR and latency p95/p99; for rerank you also want judge-based relevance. Will Redwood help set up evaluation harness?
[06:21] Marco: yes, we provide eval harness templates, and we'll run the benchmark with your queries. We'll output MRR/NDGC/latency/cost per q. We'll also show token-level cost breakdowns for Hosted embedding generation if you use our embeddings.
[06:34] Priya: ok this is all high level - can we go through a proposed pilot plan and what Redwood needs?
[06:40] Sophie: Pilot plan suggested: 1) Fulcrum provides 200k vector sample and 500-1000 queries + judge labels; 2) Redwood ingests sample into a Dedicated pilot cluster (or uses a hosted transient env if you prefer); 3) run index variants (HNSW float32, IVFPQ 8-bit, PQ), run embedding dims 1536/1024/768, measure recall/latency/cost; 4) run rerank experiments with cross-encoder on GPU and optimized batching; 5) produce a report and recommend production config.
[07:05] Asha: timeline?
[07:06] Sophie: if you can deliver sample by 2026-07-06, we can run pilot in week of 2026-07-13 and deliver results by 2026-07-20.
[07:15] Tom: security again - we need SOC2 docs, encryption at rest, KMS integration. Also need to confirm where logs live and whether PII can be redacted.
[07:25] Marco: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs; KMS integrations supported for Private and Dedicated; Hosted uses customer-managed keys in some regions - we'll share specific security matrix. Log retention and redaction controls are configurable, and we can route logs to your logging account for compliance.
[07:40] Priya: pricing question: what drives cost most - tokens for embeddings or per-query ANN cost?
[07:46] Sophie: for many customers embedding generation token cost dominates early. At scale, inference compute (dedicated GPUs, index memory, and replica counts) drives fixed cost. Hosted costs are pay-as-you-go per-embedding + per-query compute; Dedicated is reserved capacity priced for predictable qps. We'll send a cost model and example numbers based on your 800 qps spikes and 3-10M vector size.
[08:06] Asha: any gotchas on dimensionality change? If we move from 1536 to 1024 will we need to reindex everything?
[08:12] Marco: yes, changing embedding dimension requires re-embedding and reindexing. That's why the pilot includes a dim sweep. Some customers keep dual indices temporarily during migration. We can help with delta-reindex tooling to minimize disruption.
[08:25] Priya: what about cold-start latency and caching?
[08:28] Marco: we support prefix/KV caching for common queries and can warm caches during deployment. Dedicated clustering also helps reduce cold tails.
[08:35] Tom: are there SLOs for Dedicated?
[08:38] Sophie: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on the contract. We'll outline typical p95/p99 targets in the sizing doc.
[08:46] Priya: ok last question - team access and permissions. We need RBAC and SSO integration.
[08:51] Marco: SSO/SAML and granular RBAC supported; for Private we can integrate with your identity provider directly. We'll include role templates for infra/dev/data-science in the onboarding docs.
[09:05] Sophie: great - next steps recap: we'll send pricing, share security and SOC2 docs, Marco will send the benchmark sheet, and you (Asha/Tom) will provide a 200k sample and queries. We'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark run week of 7/13.
[09:20] Priya: sounds good. Anything else from your side?
[09:23] Asha: just one nit - when you say "quantized indices" do you support int4? we've had data corruption issues with some open-source PQ implementations.
[09:31] Marco: we currently support 8-bit and 4-bit quantized execution paths on select kernels - the runtime chooses the safe path. We'll test quality carefully in the pilot to avoid corruption.
[09:43] Tom: also, can we get an estimate for initial Dedicated pool size? rough numbers are fine.
[09:48] Sophie: we'll run a quick sizing calc after you share qps pattern - but rough estimate for 800 peak qps with 1536 dims and 3-5M vectors might be 2-3 GPUs with appropriate memory and replicas for HA. We'll send a range in the pricing email.
[10:05] Priya: ok let's do it. Thanks Sophie and Marco.
[10:08] Sophie: thanks everyone - we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the benchmark.
[10:12] (call ends)
